dedupe_keys.name: california environmental data exchange network ceden water quality and habitat data

description: The California Environmental Data Exchange Network is the state's central place to find and share information on the condition of its water bodies, covering streams, lakes, rivers and the coastal ocean. Many groups in California monitor water quality, aquatic habitat and wildlife health, and CEDEN aggregates their results and makes them available to environmental managers and the public. The home page points to data access, data templates for submitters, integrated report data and the CEDEN 2.0 interface, and gives a contact address at the water boards. Coverage: California water bodies, at monitoring-station level, with contributors ranging from state and regional boards to volunteer groups. Access: free web access; the licence is not stated on the page read, and the query interface and record counts were not examined. Caveats: monitoring is uneven across regions and programmes, and this record rests on the home page only. It supports receiving-water quality analysis for wastewater discharge, stormwater runoff and drinking water source-protection scenarios, and complements the national Water Quality Portal record in the catalogue.
